commits.message:
fix(email-routing): point HERMES_REQUIREMENTS_MAILBOX at the real jobs@ inbox

Jobfynder split from one shared inbox into two dedicated mailboxes
(jobs@jobfynder.com for requirements, hotlists@jobfynder.com for
hotlists) on 2026-08-28, but HERMES_REQUIREMENTS_MAILBOX was never
updated to match -- it was still unset in production, defaulting to
the placeholder requirements@jobfynder.com from the old single-inbox
design. classify_recipient_mailbox() therefore never recognized
jobs@jobfynder.com and every email sent there fell through to
content-only classification instead of resolving instantly and
reliably from the recipient address.

In practice this meant: recipient routing was silently broken for
every jobs@ email since the mailbox split, though most still got
parsed correctly via the content-based fallback -- confirmed by
checking idempotency_keys against the real Inbox, several real
requirement/hotlist emails from 2026-08-27 and earlier were never
even queued at all (a separate, pre-existing gap in webhook/
subscription coverage from before the split, not something this
config fix touches).

Fix: set HERMES_REQUIREMENTS_MAILBOX=jobs@jobfynder.com and
HERMES_HOTLIST_MAILBOX=hotlists@jobfynder.com explicitly in
production .env (already applied and restarted live), and update
.env.example's stale "single shared inbox, do NOT set to
jobs@jobfynder.com" guidance to match -- it explicitly said to make
this exact change once the mailbox split happened.

Updates the three regression scripts whose assertions baked in the
old requirements@jobfynder.com placeholder:
- hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py / hermes-850-email-integration-
  check.py: point their single-recipient routing assertions at
  jobs@jobfynder.com.
- hermes-850-email-integration-check.py's shared_mailbox_check():
  the "no recipient signal" scenario it modeled (both kinds arriving
  at one shared inbox) no longer exists now that routing works;
  repurposed to test the case that actually is still ambiguous today
  -- an email addressed to both jobs@ and hotlists@ at once -- so the
  confidence-based classification fallback this test exists to cover
  still gets exercised.
- hermes-850-gmail-graph-provider-check.py: same placeholder-address
  fix in its Graph-message-normalization fixture.

Verified: full hermes-850-* regression suite green against a freshly
reset schema, live classify_recipient_mailbox() check against prod
config, hermes-api/hermes-graph-consumer restarted with zero
downtime.
